label: thm:informal-A
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:informal-A}
Fix an order $d$ at which the quotient Boolean moment SDP of
\cref{sec:degeneracy} has a unique rank-one optimum and at least one
strictly complementary optimal SOS certificate.
Then, for every fixed admissible step choice, the canonical DR residual
satisfies a uniform local error bound around its entire fixed-point set;
consequently, exact ADMM, exact sGS--ADMM, and fixed-step PDHG converge
eventually linearly from every initialization, and the limiting KKT point
they select need not be strictly complementary. Moreover, outside a
lower-dimensional semialgebraic exceptional set in the $2^n$-dimensional
space of Boolean objectives, both hypotheses hold simultaneously at every
uniquely rank-one exact order. The formal statements are
\cref{thm:boolean-fixed,thm:main}, with rates in \cref{cor:admm,cor:pdhg}.
head: environment
name: Benign degeneracy, informal

title: Notation
body_md:
All spaces are finite-dimensional and real. $\mathbb S^p$ is the space of
symmetric $p\times p$ matrices with the trace inner product
$\langle H_1,H_2\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(H_1H_2)$, Frobenius norm $\lVert \cdot\rVert_F$, and PSD cone
$\mathbb S_+^p$; $\Pi_+$ is the Frobenius projection onto $\mathbb S_+^p$ and
$\Pi_-:=\mathrm{Id}-\Pi_+$. For $S\subseteq[n]$, $x^S:=\prod_{i\in S}x_i$; optima
carry star subscripts ($x_\star$, $X_\star$), optimal sets are calligraphic
($\mathcal S_\star$, $\mathcal Z_\star$), and we distinguish the number of Boolean variables $n$,
a general SDP matrix size $p$, and the moment matrix size $N_d$ (with
$p=N_d$ in the Boolean specialization). The remaining conventions are
standard---directional derivatives $F'(z;h)$; tangent and normal cones
$T_C(z)$, $N_C(z)$; $\operatorname{ri}$, $\operatorname{aff}$, $\operatorname{cl}$; vector Euclidean and operator
norms---and are collected in \cref{app:spectral}.

label: rem:gauge
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:gauge}
A unique Boolean minimizer genuinely restricts symmetric models, since a
MAX-CUT or zero-field Ising objective satisfies $f(x)=f(-x)$ and its
minimizers come in $\pm$ pairs. Such models enter our framework after a standard gauge
fixing, such as fixing one spin in a connected instance; we use them as
motivation rather than as literal instances.

label: prop:degeneracy
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:degeneracy}
For the independent encoding $\mathcal A_d$, primal nondegeneracy of
$X_\star$~\cite{alizadeh9mp-complementarity-nondegeneracy} holds if and only
if $m=N$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dimL}
  \dim L=m-N=\frac{N(N-1)}2-|\mathcal I_{2d}|+1 .
\end{equation}
At $d=1$ one has $m=N$; at every $2\le d\le n$ one has $m>N$
(indeed $w_1w_1^\top-w_2w_2^\top\in L\setminus\{0\}$), so the rank-one
primal optimum is degenerate. If, in addition, $\mathcal S_\star$ contains a
\emph{strictly complementary} certificate $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$, i.e.\
$\operatorname{rank}(S_{\mathrm{sc}})=N-1$, then $\operatorname{aff}\mathcal S_\star=S_{\mathrm{sc}}+L$, so $\mathcal S_\star$ is
positive-dimensional with $\dim\mathcal S_\star=m-N$.

label: thm:rigidity
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Rigidity of the canonical residual field

title: Proof
body_md:
We argue by contradiction: suppose endpoints $\bar Z_k=X_\star-\sigma\bar
S_k$ and unit normals $H_k\in N_{\mathcal Z_\star}(\bar Z_k)$ satisfy
$\delta_\sigma'(\bar Z_k;H_k)\to0$, and set $E_k:=\Pi_+'(\bar Z_k;H_k)$.
\emph{First}, the certificate kills the $V$ block: $P_VE_kP_V$ is PSD by
\eqref{eq:positive-deriv}, and
$\langle P_VE_kP_V,S_{\mathrm{sc}}\rangle=\langle \mathsf P E_k,S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S_k\rangle\to0$ by
\eqref{eq:EF-identities}, so $P_VE_kP_V\to0$. \emph{Second}, the remainder
of $E_k$ has no $VV$ component, so \cref{lem:stable-directions} pushes it
to relative-interior endpoints, where the modulus $\mu_{\mathrm{ri}}$
forces it to vanish; hence $E_k\to0$, and $H_k$ approaches
$L=\mathcal R\cap\mathbb S(V)$. \emph{Third}, decomposing $H_k=Y_k+G_k$ by
\eqref{eq:normal-sum} with the bounds of \cref{lem:normal-bound} gives
$\langle H_k,Y_k\rangle\to0$ and $\limsup_k\langle H_k,G_k\rangle\le0$, contradicting
$\lVert H_k\rVert_F=1$.
The full proof is in \cref{app:rigidity-i}.

\begin{corollary}[Qualitative rigidity on $L^\perp$]\label{cor:qualitative}
Under the assumptions of \cref{thm:rigidity},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qualitative}
 \delta_\sigma'(\bar Z;H)\ne0
 \qquad\text{for every }\bar Z\in\mathcal Z_\star,\ H\in L^\perp\setminus\{0\},
\end{equation}
since $L^\perp\subseteq N_{\mathcal Z_\star}(\bar Z)$ by \eqref{eq:normal-sum}.
\end{corollary}

label: prop:eventual
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:eventual}
At $d=n$ the moment body $\mathcal X_n$ is the affine image, with unique
coefficients, of the probability simplex on $\{\pm1\}^n$:
$X=\sum_{a\in\{\pm1\}^n}\pi_a\,b_n(a)b_n(a)^\top$ with $\pi_a\ge0$,
$\sum_a\pi_a=1$. Consequently every uniquely minimized $f$ is uniquely
rank-one exact at $d=n$, so $d_\star(f)\le n$; and unique rank-one exactness
persists upward from any order at which it holds. Moreover, for every
uniquely minimized $f$ the full-order relaxation admits a strictly
complementary optimal certificate, of rank $2^n-1$, given explicitly in
\cref{app:full-order}.

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
There exists an open dense semialgebraic set $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}\subseteq\mathcal P_n$ whose
complement has Lebesgue measure zero such that every $f\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}$ has a
unique Boolean minimizer, $d_\star(f)\le n$ is well defined, and at every
order $d_\star(f)\le d\le n$ the moment relaxation has the unique optimum
$b_d(x_\star)b_d(x_\star)^\top$ and an optimal certificate of rank $N_d-1$.
Consequently, for every such $f$, every such order $d$, and every fixed
admissible parameter choice, the conclusions of
\cref{thm:boolean-fixed,cor:admm,cor:pdhg} hold: the three splitting
methods converge eventually linearly from every initialization.
head: environment
name: Generic benign degeneracy

title: Proof
body_md:
\Cref{prop:simultaneous} (\cref{app:ambient}) constructs $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}$ as above;
for $f\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}$ and $d\in[d_\star(f),n]$ the hypotheses of
\cref{thm:boolean-fixed} hold and \cref{sec:algorithms} applies; no
parameter-dependent exceptional set is needed, because the modulus
argument of \cref{sec:boolean} covers every fixed $\sigma>0$.
head: environment

title: Open problems
body_md:
First, a \emph{quantitative} rigidity: our proof produces $\mu_{\mathrm{nor}}$,
$c_\sigma$, and $t_\sigma$ by compactness; we conjecture that for the
Boolean class they admit explicit instance-parameter bounds---the missing
step from rate separation to complexity separation. Second, \emph{beyond
the Boolean quotient}: identify the weakest algebraic structure under which
one strictly complementary certificate rigidifies the entire residual
field; constrained binary hierarchies with localizing matrices are the
natural first target. We believe residual-field rigidity is the right
abstraction for exact relaxations whose certificates, rather than
solutions, are degenerate, and we hope it extends well beyond the Boolean
cube.

label: prop:encoding
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Exact standard SDP encoding

title: Proof
body_md:
The $F_{A,B}$ form a basis of $\mathbb S^N$. Within one XOR class, $\mathcal G_d$ maps
each basis element to the same monomial, so its kernel in that class
consists of coefficient vectors summing to zero, with basis given by
differences from the reference pair; distinct classes have disjoint
supports. This proves the kernel assertion and independence of the $D_i$.
Since $\mathcal G_d(E_{\emptyset,\emptyset})=1$, the normalization row is not in
their span, so $\mathcal A_d$ has full row rank. The equalities $\mathcal A_dX=e_1$ state
that the entries of $X$ are constant on each XOR class with common
diagonal equal to one, which is the affine-set identity; its direction space
is $\mathcal T_d$, and orthogonal complementation gives the row space. Finally
$I_N\in\mathcal R_d$ (matrices in $\mathcal T_d$ have zero diagonal) and $\mathcal A_dI_N=e_1$,
so $I_N$ is the unique feasible point of $\operatorname{ran}(\mathcal A_d^*)$, namely
$\mathcal A_d^\dagger e_1$.

label: lem:slack-trace
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Trace identity and compactness

title: Proof
body_md:
$\operatorname{tr} S=\langle A_\emptyset,S\rangle$ is the constant coefficient of $\mathcal G_d(S)=f-f_\star$,
which is $f_\emptyset-f_\star$. The set is closed, and
$\lVert S\rVert_F\le\operatorname{tr} S$ for PSD matrices, so it is bounded.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the constant-diagonal identity \eqref{eq:transverse-intersection},
$\ker(\mathcal A_d)\cap\mathbb S(V)^\perp=\mathcal T_d\cap\mathbb S(V)^\perp=\{0\}$, so $\mathcal A_d$ is
injective on the $N$-dimensional tangent space
\eqref{eq:nondeg-definition}; hence nondegeneracy holds if and only if
$m=N$.
For the dimension formula, $\mathcal R_d+\mathbb S(V)=\mathbb S^N$ because the orthogonal
complement of the sum is $\mathcal T_d\cap\mathbb S(V)^\perp=\{0\}$; therefore
\[
 \dim L=\dim\bigl(\mathcal R_d\cap\mathbb S(V)\bigr)
 =m+\frac{(N-1)N}2-\frac{N(N+1)}2=m-N,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:dimL} by \eqref{eq:Ad}. At $d=1$, $N=n+1$ and
$|\mathcal I_2|=1+n+\binom n2$, so
$m=\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}2-\binom n2-n-1+1=n+1=N$. For $d\ge2$, the two Gram
vectors $w_1=e_\emptyset-a\,e_{\{i,j\}}$ and $w_2=e_{\{i\}}-a\,e_{\{j\}}$ of
\cref{sec:degeneracy} are orthogonal to $u$ and represent the same
polynomial \eqref{eq:same-poly}, so
$w_1w_1^\top-w_2w_2^\top$ is a nonzero element of
$\mathbb S(V)\cap\mathcal H_d^\perp=L$ by \eqref{eq:boolean-L}; hence $\dim L\ge1$ and
$m>N$. For the final clause, \cref{lem:slack-slice} gives
$\mathcal S_\star=(S_{\mathrm{sc}}+L)\cap\mathbb S_+(V)$ with $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$ positive definite on $V$, so a
relative neighborhood of $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$ in $S_{\mathrm{sc}}+L$ stays inside $\mathcal S_\star$; hence
$\operatorname{aff}\mathcal S_\star=S_{\mathrm{sc}}+L$ and $\dim\mathcal S_\star=\dim L=m-N$.
head: environment

title: Conventions
body_md:
If $E\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ is a subspace with orthogonal projector $P_E$, then
$\mathbb S(E):=\{H\in\mathbb S^p:H=P_EHP_E\}$ and
$\mathbb S_+(E):=\mathbb S(E)\cap\mathbb S_+^p$; the complement $\mathbb S(E)^\perp$ is taken in
$\mathbb S^p$. For a nonempty closed convex set $C$ and $z\in C$,
\[
 T_C(z):=\{h:\exists t_k\downarrow0,\ z_k\in C,\ (z_k-z)/t_k\to h\},
 \qquad
 N_C(z):=\{h:\langle h,w-z\rangle\le0\ \forall w\in C\},
\]
and $N_C(z):=\emptyset$ for $z\notin C$; $\operatorname{ri}$, $\operatorname{aff}$, and $\operatorname{cl}$ denote
relative interior, affine hull, and closure. Vectors take the Euclidean
norm $\lVert \cdot\rVert_2$, and $\lVert \cdot\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}$ is the operator norm.
Directional derivatives are
$F'(z;h):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}(F(z+th)-F(z))/t$, positively homogeneous in
$h$ but not necessarily linear. For a linear map $B:E_1\to E_2$ between
Euclidean spaces with $E_1\ne\{0\}$, set
$\sigma_{\min}(B):=\min_{\|h\|=1}\|Bh\|$; it is positive if and only if $B$ is
injective, and
$|\sigma_{\min}(B_1)-\sigma_{\min}(B_2)|\le\lVert B_1-B_2\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}$.

label: lem:drs
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:drs}
$T_{\sigma,1}$ is the DR map, with the PSD projection first, for
$F(X)=\langle C,X\rangle+\iota_{\{\mathcal A X=b\}}(X)$ and $G=\iota_{\mathbb S_+^p}$. Its fixed
points decode KKT points via $X=\Pi_+(Z)$, $S=-\sigma^{-1}\Pi_-(Z)$. In
particular, if the primal optimizer $X_\star$ is unique, then
$\mathcal Z_\star:=\operatorname{Fix} T_{\sigma,1}=\{X_\star-\sigma S:S\in\mathcal S_\star\}$, where $\mathcal S_\star$ is
the optimal slack set.
head: environment
name: DR and KKT encoding

title: Proof
body_md:
The affine proximal map is
$\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma F}(W)=X_b+\mathsf P^\perp(W-\sigma C)$. Substituting it
into $Z^+=Z+\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma F}(2\Pi_+(Z)-Z)-\Pi_+(Z)$ gives
\eqref{eq:res-components}; this is the standard DR
construction~\cite{eckstein92mp-drs,bauschke17springer-convex-analysis-hilbert-spaces}.
The Moreau decomposition of $Z$ gives $X:=\Pi_+(Z)\succeq0$,
$S:=-\sigma^{-1}\Pi_-(Z)\succeq0$, and $XS=0$. The two orthogonal equations
$r^{\parallel}=r^{\perp}_\sigma=0$ are equivalent to $\mathcal A X=b$ and
$C-S\in\operatorname{ran}(\mathcal A^*)$, hence to KKT feasibility plus complementarity;
surjectivity of $\mathcal A$ makes the multiplier unique. Conversely any KKT pair
$(X,S)$ gives the fixed point $Z=X-\sigma S$. When the primal optimizer is
unique, this gives the fixed-point identity stated in \cref{lem:drs}.
head: environment

label: lem:slack-slice
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:slack-slice}
Under \cref{ass:one-sided},
$\mathcal S_\star=(S_{\mathrm{sc}}+L)\cap\mathbb S_+(V)$ with $L:=\mathcal R\cap\mathbb S(V)=\operatorname{span}(\mathcal S_\star-\mathcal S_\star)$.
Consequently $\mathcal Z_\star$ is compact and convex with affine direction space $L$,
$S_{\mathrm{sc}}\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal S_\star$, and every $S\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal S_\star$ is positive definite on $V$.
head: environment
name: Optimal affine slice

title: Proof
body_md:
Any optimal slack is complementary to $X_\star$, hence supported on $V$;
subtracting its dual equality from that of $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$ shows
$S-S_{\mathrm{sc}}\in\mathcal R$, proving $\mathcal S_\star\subseteq(S_{\mathrm{sc}}+L)\cap\mathbb S_+(V)$. Conversely
$S=S_{\mathrm{sc}}+H\succeq0$ with $H\in\mathcal R\cap\mathbb S(V)$ is dual feasible and
complementary to the feasible $X_\star$, hence optimal. For every such $H$,
$S_{\mathrm{sc}}\pm tH$ is positive definite on $V$ for small $t>0$, so these
directions span the affine hull, $L=\operatorname{span}(\mathcal S_\star-\mathcal S_\star)$, and
$S_{\mathrm{sc}}\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal S_\star$. If $S\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal S_\star$, extending the segment from $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$
through $S$ slightly stays in $\mathcal S_\star$, so $S$ is a convex combination with
positive weight on $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$ and is positive definite on $V$. The assertions
for $\mathcal Z_\star=X_\star-\sigma\mathcal S_\star$ follow from the affine bijection.
head: environment

label: lem:sylvester
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sylvester}
Set $X_U:=B_U^\top X_\star B_U=\Lambda_U\succ0$ and
$\bar S_V:=B_V^\top\bar SB_V\succeq0$. For $H\in\mathbb S^p$, put
$H^0_{UU}:=B_U^\top HB_U$, $M:=B_U^\top HB_V$, $H^0_{VV}:=B_V^\top HB_V$.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:coarse-derivative}
 [B_U\ B_V]^\top\,\Pi_+'(\bar Z;H)\,[B_U\ B_V]
 =\begin{bmatrix}H^0_{UU}&Y\\Y^\top&
 O_K\Pi_+(O_K^\top H^0_{VV}O_K)O_K^\top\end{bmatrix},
 \qquad
 X_UY+\sigma Y\bar S_V=X_UM .
\end{equation}
The operator $\mathscr L_{\bar S}:Y\mapsto X_UY+\sigma Y\bar S_V$ is
invertible with
$\|\mathscr L_{\bar S}^{-1}\|_{F\to F}\le a_U^{-1}$,
$a_U:=\lambda_{\min}(X_U)>0$, uniformly in $\bar S\in\mathcal S_\star$.
head: environment
name: Sylvester form in fixed coarse coordinates

title: Proof
body_md:
In eigencoordinates the Sylvester equation reads
$(\xi_i+\sigma s_j)\widetilde Y_{ij}=\xi_i\widetilde M_{ij}$, allowing
$s_j=0$ on $K$; this reproduces the $UK$ and $UJ$ blocks of
\eqref{eq:positive-deriv}, and the $VV$ block is the displayed
$K$-embedding. For every $Y$,
$\langle Y,\mathscr L_{\bar S}Y\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(Y^\top X_UY)+\sigma\operatorname{tr}(Y^\top Y\bar S_V)
\ge a_U\lVert Y\rVert_F^2$, and Cauchy--Schwarz gives
$\lVert \mathscr L_{\bar S}Y\rVert_F\ge a_U\lVert Y\rVert_F$; injectivity in equal finite
dimensions gives invertibility and the bound.
head: environment

label: prop:cones
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Endpoint cones

title: Proof
body_md:
For the cone supported on $V$, the tangent and ambient normal formulas are
\[
 T_{\mathbb S_+(V)}(\bar S)=\{H\in\mathbb S(V):Q_K^\top HQ_K\succeq0\},
 \qquad
 N_{\mathbb S_+(V)}(\bar S)=\mathbb S(V)^\perp-\mathcal K(\bar S).
\]
For completeness: the tangent condition is necessary by evaluating feasible
secants on vectors of $\ker(\bar S)\cap V$; it is sufficient because adding
$\varepsilon P_K$ to a direction makes its $KK$ block positive definite, after
which the Schur complement shows $\bar S+t(H+\varepsilon P_K)$ is PSD for small
$t>0$, and $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ closes the cone. The normal formula is the
polar: the free $KJ$ and $JJ$ tangent blocks force the corresponding normal
blocks to vanish, and the polar of the PSD $KK$ cone is its negative.
For the affine slice $\mathcal S_\star=(S_{\mathrm{sc}}+L)\cap\mathbb S_+(V)$, the same approximation
can be performed \emph{inside $L$}: replace $H$ by $H+\varepsilon(S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S)$,
whose $KK$ block is positive definite because $S_{\mathrm{sc}}\succ0$ on $V$; this
proves \eqref{eq:slack-tangent}. The relative Slater point $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$ justifies
the normal-cone intersection rule~\cite{rockafellar15book-convex-analysis},
so
$N_{\mathcal S_\star}(\bar S)=L^\perp+\mathbb S(V)^\perp-\mathcal K(\bar S)=L^\perp-\mathcal K(\bar S)$,
using $L\subseteq\mathbb S(V)$. Finally the affine bijection
$S\mapsto X_\star-\sigma S$ maps tangents by $-\sigma$ and normals by
$-\sigma^{-1}$; positive scalars do not change cones, and the sign flip
gives \eqref{eq:shadow-tangent}--\eqref{eq:shadow-normal}.

label: lem:psd-cauchy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:psd-cauchy}
If $S\succeq0$ and $B_E,B_F$ are orthonormal frames for orthogonal
subspaces, then
$\lVert B_E^\top SB_F\rVert_F^2\le\operatorname{tr}(B_E^\top SB_E)\,\operatorname{tr}(B_F^\top SB_F)$.
head: environment
name: PSD off-block bound

title: Proof
body_md:
The block is $(S^{1/2}B_E)^\top(S^{1/2}B_F)$, so
$\lVert B_E^\top SB_F\rVert_F\le\lVert S^{1/2}B_E\rVert_F\,\lVert S^{1/2}B_F\rVert_F$; square and
use $\lVert S^{1/2}B_E\rVert_F^2=\operatorname{tr}(B_E^\top SB_E)$, likewise for $B_F$.
head: environment

label: lem:pv-bound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pv-bound}
Let $W\in\mathbb S_+^p$ and let $P_V$ be the orthogonal projector onto a
subspace $V\subseteq\mathbb R^p$. Then $W\succeq aP_V$ for some $a>0$ if and only
if $V\subseteq\operatorname{ran}(W)$; in that case, when $W\ne0$, one may take $a=\lambda_+(W)$, the
smallest positive eigenvalue of $W$.
head: environment
name: Projection lower bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Necessity: if $W\succeq aP_V$ and $z\in\ker(W)$, then
$0=z^\top Wz\ge a\lVert P_Vz\rVert_2^2$, so $P_Vz=0$; hence $\ker(W)\perp V$,
i.e.\ $V\subseteq\ker(W)^\perp=\operatorname{ran}(W)$. Sufficiency: for every $x$,
$x^\top Wx\ge\lambda_+(W)\lVert P_{\operatorname{ran}(W)}x\rVert_2^2$, and $V\subseteq\operatorname{ran}(W)$
gives $\lVert P_{\operatorname{ran}(W)}x\rVert_2\ge\lVert P_Vx\rVert_2$, so
$x^\top Wx\ge\lambda_+(W)\,x^\top P_Vx$.
head: environment

label: rem:pv
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:pv}
The condition $V\subseteq\operatorname{ran}(W)$ in \cref{lem:pv-bound} cannot be replaced
by ``$W$ is positive definite on $V$'', which only says
$V\cap\ker(W)=\{0\}$. For
$W=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ and
$V=\operatorname{span}\{e_1\}$, the quadratic form $(te_1)^\top W(te_1)=t^2$ is
positive on $V$, yet $\det(W-aP_V)=-a<0$ for every $a>0$, so no inequality
$W\succeq aP_V$ holds. In \cref{lem:normal-bound} the stronger condition is
available because $\operatorname{ran}(S_{\mathrm{sc}})=V$.
head: environment
name: Positive definiteness on $V$ is not enough

label: lem:normal-bound
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Uniformly bounded normal decompositions

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $W\succeq0$, $\operatorname{tr} W\ge\lVert W\rVert_F$. Because $W$ is supported on $V$ and
$S_{\mathrm{sc}}\succeq a_sP_V$---by \cref{lem:pv-bound}, since $\operatorname{ran}(S_{\mathrm{sc}})=V$ and
$a_s$ is the smallest positive eigenvalue of $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$---and because
$\bar SW=0$ and $S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S\in L$,
\[
 a_s\lVert W\rVert_F\le a_s\operatorname{tr} W\le\langle W,S_{\mathrm{sc}}\rangle
 =\langle W,S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S\rangle
 =\langle H,S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S\rangle
 \le\lVert H\rVert_F\,\lVert S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S\rVert_F.
\]
The bound on $Y=H-W$ follows, compactness of $\mathcal S_\star$ bounds the factor, and
$H=0$ gives the intersection statement.
head: environment

label: lem:stable-directions
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Boundary-stable directions

title: Proof
body_md:
The relative-interior assertion follows from
$\bar S_\varepsilon\succ0$ on $V$ and \cref{lem:slack-slice}. For the convergence,
use the coarse form \eqref{eq:coarse-derivative}: the $VV$ block of
$\Pi_+'(\cdot;G)$ vanishes because $G^0_{VV}=B_V^\top GB_V=0$, and the cross
block is $Y_\varepsilon=\mathscr L_{\bar S_\varepsilon}^{-1}(X_UM)$ with
$M=B_U^\top GB_V$. Moreover
\[
 \|\mathscr L_{\bar S_\varepsilon}-\mathscr L_{\bar S}\|_{F\to F}
 \le\sigma\lVert \bar S_\varepsilon-\bar S\rVert_2,\qquad
 \|\mathscr L_{\bar S_\varepsilon}^{-1}\|_{F\to F},\
 \|\mathscr L_{\bar S}^{-1}\|_{F\to F}\le a_U^{-1}
\]
by \cref{lem:sylvester}, so the inverse identity
$B^{-1}-A^{-1}=B^{-1}(A-B)A^{-1}$ gives $Y_\varepsilon\to Y$. Hence both projection
derivatives converge along $G$, and \eqref{eq:res-deriv} gives
\eqref{eq:stable-directions}. The hypothesis concerns the \emph{entire fixed
$VV$ block} rather than only the kernel block at one endpoint; it removes the term
that jumps when the kernel grows.
head: environment

label: eq:vanishing-components
title: Proof
body_md:
If the full-normal modulus were zero, compactness would allow endpoints
$\bar Z_k=X_\star-\sigma\bar S_k$ and unit normals
$H_k\in N_{\mathcal Z_\star}(\bar Z_k)$ such that, after a subsequence,
$\bar Z_k\to\bar Z$, $H_k\to H$, and
$\lVert \delta_\sigma'(\bar Z_k;H_k)\rVert_F\to0$.
Set $E_k:=\Pi_+'(\bar Z_k;H_k)$ and $F_k:=\Pi_-'(\bar Z_k;H_k)$. These are
bounded, $E_k+F_k=H_k$, and \eqref{eq:res-deriv} yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:vanishing-components}
 \mathsf P E_k\to0,\qquad \mathsf P^\perp F_k\to0 ,
\end{equation}
whence $\langle E_k,F_k\rangle\to0$ by splitting the inner product along
$\mathcal R\oplus\mathcal N$.

\emph{Step 1.} The ambient $V$-supported block $E_k^V:=P_VE_kP_V$ is PSD by
\eqref{eq:positive-deriv}, and
$\langle E_k^V,S_{\mathrm{sc}}\rangle=\langle E_k,S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S_k\rangle
=\langle \mathsf P E_k,S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S_k\rangle\to0$,
using $\langle E_k,\bar S_k\rangle=0$ and $S_{\mathrm{sc}}-\bar S_k\in L\subseteq\mathcal R$. Since
$S_{\mathrm{sc}}\succ0$ on $V$, it follows that $E_k^V\to0$.

\emph{Step 2.} Let $W_k:=E_k-E_k^V\in\mathbb S(V)^\perp\subseteq L^\perp$. Using
the endpoint eigenbasis $Q_k$ only for this calculation,
\eqref{eq:positive-deriv} gives $\Pi_+'(\bar Z_k;W_k)=W_k+R_k$ and
$\Pi_-'(\bar Z_k;W_k)=-R_k$,
where $R_k$ has only $UJ_k$ and $J_kU$ blocks and
$(\widetilde R_k)_{UJ_k}=-\Omega_k\circ(\mathbf1-\Omega_k)
\circ(\widetilde H_k)_{UJ_k}$. By \eqref{eq:EF-identities},
$\lVert R_k\rVert_F^2\le\langle E_k,F_k\rangle\to0$. Since $\mathsf P W_k\to0$ as well,
$\delta_\sigma'(\bar Z_k;W_k)\to0$. If $W_k$ did not converge to zero,
restrict to a subsequence with $\lVert W_k\rVert_F\ge c>0$; each $W_k$ satisfies
$P_VW_kP_V=0$, so by \cref{lem:stable-directions} we may choose
$0<\varepsilon_k\le1/k$ with
$\delta_\sigma'(X_\star-\sigma\bar S_{k,\varepsilon_k};W_k)\to0$ and
$\bar S_{k,\varepsilon_k}\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal S_\star$.
Positive homogeneity and the uniform modulus \eqref{eq:mu-def} imply
$\lVert \delta_\sigma'(X_\star-\sigma\bar S_{k,\varepsilon_k};W_k)\rVert_F
\ge\mu_{\mathrm{ri}}\lVert W_k\rVert_F$, a contradiction. Thus
$E_k=W_k+E_k^V\to0$.

\emph{Step 3.} Now \eqref{eq:vanishing-components} gives
$\operatorname{dist}_F(H_k,\mathcal R)\to0$. Also $\operatorname{dist}_F(H_k,\mathbb S(V))\to0$: the $UU$ block of
$H_k$ equals that of $E_k$, and the fixed-coordinate Sylvester identity of
\cref{lem:sylvester} gives
$M_k=Y_k^c+\sigma X_U^{-1}Y_k^c(\bar S_k)_V$, with
$M_k=B_U^\top H_kB_V$ and $Y_k^c=B_U^\top E_kB_V$,
and the right side tends to zero because $(\bar S_k)$ is bounded and
$Y_k^c\to0$. The fixed subspaces $\mathcal R$ and $\mathbb S(V)$ therefore give
$\operatorname{dist}_F(H_k,L)\to0$: both distance functions are invariant under
translations along $L$, so the claim reduces to positivity of the minimum
of $\operatorname{dist}_F(\cdot,\mathcal R)+\operatorname{dist}_F(\cdot,\mathbb S(V))$ on the unit sphere of
$L^\perp$, and a zero there would produce a unit vector of $L^\perp$ inside
$\mathcal R\cap\mathbb S(V)=L$.

\emph{Step 4.} Choose $\ell_k\in L$ with $H_k-\ell_k\to0$. By
\cref{prop:cones,lem:normal-bound}, write $H_k=Y_k+G_k$ with
$Y_k\in L^\perp$, $G_k\in\mathcal K(\bar S_k)$, both bounded. Then
$\langle H_k,Y_k\rangle=\langle H_k-\ell_k,Y_k\rangle\to0$. Because $G_k$ is PSD and supported
on $K_k$, spectral coordinates give
\[
 \langle H_k,G_k\rangle
 =\langle (\widetilde H_k)_{K_kK_k},(\widetilde G_k)_{K_kK_k}\rangle
 \le\langle \Pi_+((\widetilde H_k)_{K_kK_k}),(\widetilde G_k)_{K_kK_k}\rangle
 =\langle E_k^V,G_k\rangle;
\]
the inequality uses $M\preceq\Pi_+(M)$ and $G_k\succeq0$ and does not
require commutativity. Since $E_k^V\to0$ and $(G_k)$ is bounded,
$\limsup_k\langle H_k,G_k\rangle\le0$. Hence
$1=\lVert H_k\rVert_F^2=\langle H_k,Y_k\rangle+\langle H_k,G_k\rangle$ has limit superior at most
zero, a contradiction.
head: environment

label: eq:normal-radius
title: Proof
body_md:
Only \cref{ass:one-sided} and the qualitative statement
\eqref{eq:qualitative} are used. It suffices to prove: there exist
$c_\sigma,t_\sigma>0$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:normal-radius}
 \lVert \delta_\sigma(\bar Z+tH)\rVert_F\ge c_\sigma t
 \qquad\bigl(\bar Z\in\mathcal Z_\star,\ H\in N_{\mathcal Z_\star}(\bar Z),\ \lVert H\rVert_F=1,
 \ 0\le t\le t_\sigma\bigr),
\end{equation}
since for $Z$ near $\mathcal Z_\star$ its Frobenius nearest point $\bar Z$ satisfies
$Z-\bar Z\in N_{\mathcal Z_\star}(\bar Z)$ with $\lVert Z-\bar Z\rVert_F=\operatorname{dist}_F(Z,\mathcal Z_\star)$,
and conversely a normal ray has nearest point at its base.

Suppose no such constants exist. Choose
$\bar Z_k=X_\star-\sigma\bar S_k\in\mathcal Z_\star$,
$H_k\in N_{\mathcal Z_\star}(\bar Z_k)$ with $\lVert H_k\rVert_F=1$, and $0<t_k\le1/k$ with
$Z_k:=\bar Z_k+t_kH_k$ and $\lVert \delta_\sigma(Z_k)\rVert_F/t_k\to0$. Set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:secants}
 X_k:=\Pi_+(Z_k),\quad S_k:=-\sigma^{-1}\Pi_-(Z_k),\quad
 E_k:=\frac{X_k-X_\star}{t_k},\quad
 F_k:=-\sigma\,\frac{S_k-\bar S_k}{t_k}.
\end{equation}
Nonexpansiveness of the projections gives $\lVert E_k\rVert_F,\lVert F_k\rVert_F\le1$ and
$E_k+F_k=H_k$. After a subsequence,
$\bar S_k\to\bar S$, $H_k\to H$, $E_k\to E$, $F_k\to F$, with $E+F=H$ and
$\lVert H\rVert_F=1$; closedness of the normal-cone graph gives
$H\in N_{\mathcal Z_\star}(X_\star-\sigma\bar S)$. Since
$\delta_\sigma(\bar Z_k)=0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:secant-res}
 \frac{\delta_\sigma(Z_k)}{t_k}=-\mathsf P E_k-\mathsf P^\perp F_k\to0,
 \qquad\text{so}\quad \mathsf P E_k\to0,\quad \mathsf P^\perp F_k\to0,
\end{equation}
hence $E\in\mathcal N$, $F\in\mathcal R$, and $\langle E_k,F_k\rangle\to0$. These are
\emph{moving-base secants} rather than derivatives at the limiting endpoint; no
identification with $\Pi_+'(\bar Z;H)$ has been made.

Exact complementarity $X_kS_k=0$ and $X_\star\bar S_k=0$ yields the energy
identity \eqref{eq:secant-energy}; since both its terms are nonnegative and
$\langle E_k,F_k\rangle\to0$, we get $\langle X_\star,S_k\rangle=o(t_k^2)$. As $X_\star\succ0$
on the fixed $U$, $\operatorname{tr}(B_U^\top S_kB_U)=o(t_k^2)$, and
\cref{lem:psd-cauchy} with the bounded $(S_k)$ gives
$\lVert B_U^\top S_kB_V\rVert_F=o(t_k)$. Every $\bar S_k$ is supported on $V$, so
the $UU$ and $UV$ blocks of $F_k$ tend to zero, and therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:F-in-L}
 F\in\mathbb S(V)\cap\mathcal R=L .
\end{equation}

Use \cref{lem:normal-bound} to write $H_k=Y_k+G_k$ with bounded
$Y_k\in L^\perp$ and $G_k\in\mathcal K(\bar S_k)$. Equation \eqref{eq:F-in-L}
implies $\langle Y_k,F_k\rangle\to0$, while
\[
 \langle G_k,F_k\rangle
 =-\frac{\sigma}{t_k}\langle G_k,S_k-\bar S_k\rangle
 =-\frac{\sigma}{t_k}\langle G_k,S_k\rangle\le0,
\]
using $\langle G_k,\bar S_k\rangle=0$. Thus $\limsup_k\langle H_k,F_k\rangle\le0$; but
$\langle H_k,F_k\rangle=\langle E_k,F_k\rangle+\lVert F_k\rVert_F^2\ge\lVert F_k\rVert_F^2$, so $F_k\to0$
and $H=E\in\mathcal N\subseteq L^\perp$.

Finally, expanding $X_kS_k=0$ by \eqref{eq:secants} and dividing by $t_k$
gives $E_k\bar S_k-\sigma^{-1}X_\star F_k-\sigma^{-1}t_kE_kF_k=0$; passing
to the limit yields $H\bar S=0$, and symmetry gives $\bar SH=0$. Also
$P_VE_kP_V=t_k^{-1}P_VX_kP_V\succeq0$, hence $P_VHP_V\succeq0$. In the
limiting $U\oplus K\oplus J$ coordinates, $H$ therefore has zero $J$ rows
and columns and a PSD $KK$ block, so \eqref{eq:positive-deriv} gives
\[
 \Pi_+'(\bar Z;H)=H,\qquad \Pi_-'(\bar Z;H)=0,\qquad
 \delta_\sigma'(\bar Z;H)=-\mathsf P H=0 ,
\]
contradicting \eqref{eq:qualitative}, because $H\in L^\perp$ and
$\lVert H\rVert_F=1$.
head: environment

label: ex:not-abstract
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:not-abstract}
Let $\phi(s)=s^2/(1+s)$ for $s\ge0$ and
\[
 q(t)=\begin{cases}t+\phi(-t),&t<0,\\ t,&0\le t\le1,\\
 t-\phi(t-1),&t>1,\end{cases}
\]
a nondecreasing $1$-Lipschitz function, so $T(t,s)=(q(t),0)$ is firmly
nonexpansive on $\mathbb R^2$ with $\operatorname{Fix} T=[0,1]\times\{0\}$. Along
relative-interior normals $(0,h)$ the residual has derivative $(0,-h)$, so
the relative-interior modulus equals one; yet at the boundary point $(1,0)$
with outward normal $(1,0)$,
$(T-\mathrm{Id})(1+t,0)=\bigl(-t^2/(1+t),\,0\bigr)$, and the residual vanishes to
first order. Rigidity fails for this map.
head: environment
name: A firmly nonexpansive map with a flat boundary normal

label: rem:rigidity-scope
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:rigidity-scope}
The proof gives positive constants $\mu_{\mathrm{nor}},c_\sigma,t_\sigma$
for the fixed instance, but does not identify them with $\mu_{\mathrm{ri}}$
or furnish a uniform rate over objectives. The finite-radius argument is not
a uniform Taylor expansion across singular endpoints: it exploits exact PSD
complementarity of the projection secants. Likewise, knowing that each
relative-interior derivative is injective is weaker than knowing the
positive uniform infimum $\mu_{\mathrm{ri}}>0$.
head: environment
name: What rigidity does and does not assert

label: eq:boolean-lift
title: Proof
body_md:
In coordinates whose first vector is $q$, matrices of $\mathbb S(V)$ have zero
first row and column, so $\mathbb S(V)^\perp$ consists of the matrices with zero
$VV$ block, which are $\{qv^\top+vq^\top\}$; this is
\eqref{eq:Fq-perp}. If such a matrix lies in $\mathcal T_d$, its diagonal
vanishes; the diagonal entries are $2q_Av_A$ and every
$q_A=\pm N^{-1/2}\ne0$, so $v=0$, proving
\eqref{eq:transverse-intersection}. For \eqref{eq:boolean-L}, the Boolean
moment identity is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:boolean-lift}
 uu^\top=\sum_{\Gamma\in\mathcal I_{2d}}x_\star^\Gamma A_\Gamma
        =I_N+\sum_{\Gamma\ne\emptyset}x_\star^\Gamma A_\Gamma ,
\end{equation}
since $(uu^\top)_{A,B}=x_\star^Ax_\star^B=x_\star^{A\triangle B}$. If
$H\in\mathbb S(V)\cap\mathcal R_d$, then $Hu=0$ and $H\perp\mathcal T_d$, so
$0=\langle uu^\top,H\rangle=\operatorname{tr} H$ by \eqref{eq:boolean-lift}; hence $H\perp I_N$ as
well and $H\in\mathcal H_d^\perp$. The reverse inclusion is immediate because
$\mathcal T_d\subseteq\mathcal H_d$. That this space equals
$L=\operatorname{span}(\mathcal S_\star-\mathcal S_\star)$ is \cref{lem:slack-slice} under the instantiation
of \cref{sec:boolean}. Taking orthogonal complements gives
$L^\perp=\mathbb S(V)^\perp+\mathcal H_d=\mathbb S(V)^\perp+\mathcal T_d$ (subspace sums, not
orthogonal sums), the last equality because
$I_N=uu^\top-\sum_{\Gamma\neq\emptyset}x_\star^\Gamma A_\Gamma$ and
$uu^\top=N qq^\top\in\mathbb S(V)^\perp$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply \eqref{eq:positive-deriv} at $\bar Z=X_\star-\sigma S$ with the
Boolean dictionary: $U=\operatorname{span}\{q\}$ is one-dimensional with
$\Lambda_U=(N)$, so $\Omega_{1j}=N/(N+\sigma s_j)$. The $UU$ block
contributes $h_{00}qq^\top$ with $h_{00}=q^\top Hq$. The $UK$ and $UJ$
blocks assemble into $qw^\top+wq^\top$ with
\[
 w=\sum_{j}\frac{N}{N+\sigma s_j}\,q_jq_j^\top Hq
  \;+\;P_KHq
  \;=\;N(NI_N+\sigma S)^{-1}P_VHq ,
\]
since $(NI_N+\sigma S)^{-1}$ acts on $K$ as $N^{-1}P_K$ and on the
eigenvector $q_j$ of $S$ as $(N+\sigma s_j)^{-1}$; note $w\perp q$. The
$VV$ block of \eqref{eq:positive-deriv} is
$Q_K\Pi_+(Q_K^\top HQ_K)Q_K^\top$, which vanishes when $K=\{0\}$, i.e.\ when
$S\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal S_\star$ by \cref{lem:slack-slice}. This proves
\eqref{eq:true-boundary-derivative}, and \eqref{eq:interior-derivative}
follows because at interior certificates $X_\star-\sigma S$ is nonsingular,
$\Pi_+$ is differentiable there, and
$\delta_\sigma'=-\mathsf P\Pi_+'-\mathsf P^\perp\Pi_-'
=-\bigl(\mathsf P\mathscr J_S+\mathsf P^\perp(\mathrm{Id}-\mathscr J_S)\bigr)=-\Psi_S$ by
\eqref{eq:res-deriv}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $\Psi_S(H)=0$ and put $E:=\mathscr J_S(H)$, $F:=H-E$. The two residual
components vanish separately, so $E\in\mathcal T_d$ and $F\in\mathcal R_d$. But
$E\in\mathbb S(V)^\perp$ by construction, so the constant-diagonal identity
\eqref{eq:transverse-intersection} forces
\[
 E\ \in\ \mathcal T_d\cap\mathbb S(V)^\perp=\{0\}.
\]
Multiplying $E=0$ by $q$ gives $h_{00}=0$ and $w=0$; the inverse in
\eqref{eq:Jextension} is nonsingular, so $P_VHq=0$, and with $q^\top Hq=0$
this yields $Hq=0$, i.e.\ $H\in\mathbb S(V)$. Then $F=H\in\mathcal R_d$, so
$H\in\mathbb S(V)\cap\mathcal R_d=L$. Conversely $H\in L$ gives $\mathscr J_S(H)=0$ and
$\mathsf P^\perp H=0$, so $\Psi_S(H)=0$. This proves $\ker(\Psi_S)=L$; in particular
$\sigma_{\min}(\Psi_S|_{L^\perp})>0$ for each $S$ by finite dimensionality.
Continuity of $S\mapsto\Psi_S$ (\cref{app:continuity} below) makes this
least singular value continuous, and compactness of $\mathcal S_\star$ gives
$\mu_\star>0$. Finally, on $\operatorname{ri}\mathcal S_\star$ the extension coincides with the true
derivative, which gives \eqref{eq:boolean-muri}.
head: environment

label: lem:averaged-eb
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:averaged-eb}
Let $T$ be $\alpha$-averaged, $0<\alpha<1$, in a norm $\|\cdot\|_G$ with
$m\|\cdot\|^2\le\|\cdot\|_G^2\le M\|\cdot\|^2$ on a finite-dimensional
space, let $F:=\operatorname{Fix} T\ne\emptyset$, and suppose
$\|Tz-z\|\ge c\,\operatorname{dist}(z,F)$ whenever $\operatorname{dist}(z,F)\le t_0$. Then every orbit
converges to a point of $F$; it eventually enters the error-bound
neighborhood, after which $\operatorname{dist}_G(z^k,F)$ contracts Q-linearly and the
iterates converge R-linearly.
head: environment
name: Setwise error bound plus averagedness

title: Proof
body_md:
The averagedness
inequality~\cite{bauschke17springer-convex-analysis-hilbert-spaces} is
\[
 \|Tz-z_\star\|_G^2\le\|z-z_\star\|_G^2
 -\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|Tz-z\|_G^2\qquad(z_\star\in F).
\]
Taking a $G$-nearest fixed point and using norm equivalence with the error
bound gives
$\operatorname{dist}_G(Tz,F)^2\le\rho^2\operatorname{dist}_G(z,F)^2$ whenever $\operatorname{dist}(z,F)\le t_0$. The
initial condition gives $\operatorname{dist}_G(z^0,F)\le\sqrt m\,t_0$, and Fej\'er
monotonicity preserves it, so $\operatorname{dist}(z^k,F)\le t_0$ for every $k$; this
proves \eqref{eq:rate-metric} and its Euclidean form. Nonexpansiveness gives
$\|Tz-z\|_G\le2\operatorname{dist}_G(z,F)$, so the step lengths have a geometrically
summable tail and the iterates converge R-linearly to some point of $F$.
For an arbitrary starting point, averagedness gives boundedness and square
summability of $\|Tz^k-z^k\|_G$; a cluster point is fixed by continuity, and
Fej\'er monotonicity relative to it gives convergence of the whole sequence,
which therefore eventually enters the neighborhood above.
head: environment

label: prop:admm-metric
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:admm-metric}
For $0<\tau<2$, $T_{\sigma,\tau}$ is $\alpha_\tau$-averaged with
$\alpha_\tau=\max\{1,\tau\}/2$ in the metric
$\mathsf G_\tau:=\mathsf P+\tau^{-1}\mathsf P^\perp$, whose eigenvalues bound it between
$\min\{1,\tau^{-1}\}$ and $\max\{1,\tau^{-1}\}$ times the Frobenius metric.
head: environment
name: A parameter-dependent metric for the shadow map

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $T_{\sigma,\tau}=\mathrm{Id}-\mathsf D_\tau R_0$ with $R_0:=\mathrm{Id}-T_{\sigma,1}$,
which is firmly nonexpansive because the canonical DR map
is~\cite{bauschke17springer-convex-analysis-hilbert-spaces}. Put $e=Z-W$ and
$q=R_0Z-R_0W$, so $\langle e,q\rangle\ge\lVert q\rVert_F^2$. With
$\mathsf G_\tau=\mathsf D_\tau^{-1}$, self-adjointness gives
\[
 \|e-\mathsf D_\tau q\|_{\mathsf G_\tau}^2
 =\|e\|_{\mathsf G_\tau}^2-2\langle e,q\rangle+\langle q,\mathsf D_\tau q\rangle
 \le\|e\|_{\mathsf G_\tau}^2
 -\Bigl(\frac{2}{\max\{1,\tau\}}-1\Bigr)\|\mathsf D_\tau q\|_{\mathsf G_\tau}^2,
\]
using $\langle q,\mathsf D_\tau q\rangle\le\max\{1,\tau\}\lVert q\rVert_F^2\le
\max\{1,\tau\}\langle e,q\rangle$. This is the averagedness inequality with
$\alpha_\tau=\max\{1,\tau\}/2<1$ for $\tau<2$; the metric bounds are the two
eigenvalues of $\mathsf G_\tau$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Combine \eqref{eq:admm-eb}, \cref{prop:admm-metric}, and
\cref{lem:averaged-eb}: the shadow distance contracts eventually Q-linearly
in $\mathsf G_\tau$ and the shadow converges R-linearly to some
$\bar Z=X_\star-\sigma\bar S\in\mathcal Z_\star$. For the raw variables: projections
are Lipschitz, so $\Pi_+(Z^k)\to X_\star$ and $S^{k+1}\to\bar S$
R-linearly by \eqref{eq:raw-shared-S}. For ADMM, \eqref{eq:admm-filter} is a
stable linear recurrence with factor $|1-\tau|<1$, so $X^k\to X_\star$
R-linearly at any rate $\widehat\rho\in(\max\{\rho,|1-\tau|\},1)$ (the
enlargement also absorbs the $k\rho^k$ resonance when the two rates
coincide); then \eqref{eq:raw-admm-y} transfers R-linear convergence to
$\lambda^{k+1}$, whose limit is the unique multiplier of $\bar S$. For
sGS--ADMM, \eqref{eq:sgs-X} gives the exact contraction
$\mathsf P X^{k+1}-X_b=(1-\tau)(\mathsf P X^k-X_b)$, and
$\mathsf P^\perp X^k=\mathsf P^\perp Z^k+\sigma\mathsf P^\perp C$ is recovered directly from the
shadow; together with the equality-solve formulas this proves R-linear
convergence of all raw sequences. Thus convergence of the reduced shadow is
not silently substituted for convergence of the raw variables.
head: environment

label: prop:pdhg-transfer
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:pdhg-transfer}
Under surjectivity of $\mathcal A$ and $\eta_x,\eta_y>0$, the chart
\eqref{eq:pdhg-chart} is an affine bijection mapping
$\mathcal W_\star=\operatorname{Fix} T_{\mathrm P}$ onto $\mathcal Z_\star^{\eta_x}\times\{0\}$, and
\eqref{eq:pdhg-factor} holds with the linear isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pdhg-L}
 \mathscr L_{\eta_x,\eta_y}(R^\parallel,R^\perp,r)
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 R^\parallel-R^\perp-\mathcal A^\dagger r-\eta_x\eta_y\mathcal A^*(2\mathcal A R^\parallel-r)\\[1mm]
 \mathcal A R^\parallel-r
 \end{pmatrix},
 \ (R^\parallel,R^\perp,r)\in\mathcal R\times\mathcal N\times\mathbb R^m .
\end{equation}
Consequently, if the canonical residual with $\sigma=\eta_x$ satisfies
\eqref{eq:canonical-eb}, then there are $c_{\mathrm P},t_{\mathrm P}>0$ with
$\|\delta_{\mathrm P}(w)\|\ge c_{\mathrm P}\operatorname{dist}(w,\mathcal W_\star)$ whenever
$\operatorname{dist}(w,\mathcal W_\star)\le t_{\mathrm P}$, where
$\delta_{\mathrm P}:=T_{\mathrm P}-\mathrm{Id}$.
head: environment
name: Exact PDHG transfer

title: Proof
body_md:
The linear part of $\Phi$ is
$\mathsf M_\Phi=\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}\mathrm{Id}&\eta_x\mathcal A^*\\
\mathcal A&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$; if $X+\eta_x\mathcal A^*\lambda=0$ and $\mathcal A X=0$
then $\mathcal A\mathcal A^*\lambda=0$, so $\lambda=0$ and $X=0$, and the square map is
invertible, with explicit inverse
$X=X_b+\mathcal A^\dagger r+\mathsf P^\perp(Z+\eta_xC)$,
$\lambda=\eta_x^{-1}(\mathcal A\mathcal A^*)^{-1}\mathcal A(Z-X+\eta_xC)$. At a fixed point,
$\mathcal A X=b$ and $X=\Pi_+(X-\eta_xS)$ with $S=C-\mathcal A^*\lambda$---exactly the
KKT conditions---so the image of the fixed set is as claimed. Since
$X^+=\Pi_+(Z)$, decomposing by $\mathsf P,\mathsf P^\perp$ gives
\[
 X^+-X=r^{\parallel}(Z)-r^{\perp}_{\eta_x}(Z)-\mathcal A^\dagger r,\qquad
 r^+=\mathcal A\,r^{\parallel}(Z),\qquad
 \lambda^+-\lambda=\eta_y\bigl(r-2\mathcal A\,r^{\parallel}(Z)\bigr),
\]
and $Z^+-Z=X^+-X+\eta_x\mathcal A^*(\lambda^+-\lambda)$ proves
\eqref{eq:pdhg-factor}. For injectivity of $\mathscr L_{\eta_x,\eta_y}$: the
second zero component gives $r=\mathcal A R^\parallel$; substituting into the first
gives $-R^\perp-\eta_x\eta_y\mathcal A^*\mathcal A R^\parallel=0$, whose two terms lie in
the orthogonal spaces $\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal R$; hence $R^\perp=0$ and
$\mathcal A R^\parallel=0$, which forces $R^\parallel=0$ and then $r=0$. Equal
finite dimensions give the isomorphism; neither invertibility uses the
step-size inequality. Finally, let
$\ell:=\sigma_{\min}(\mathscr L_{\eta_x,\eta_y})>0$,
$a_\Phi:=\sigma_{\min}(\mathsf M_\Phi)>0$,
$b_\Phi:=\lVert \mathsf M_\Phi\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}$. Whenever
$\operatorname{dist}_F(Z,\mathcal Z_\star^{\eta_x})\le t_{\eta_x}$, orthogonality of the residual
components gives
\[
 \|\Phi T_{\mathrm P}\Phi^{-1}(Z,r)-(Z,r)\|
 \ge\ell\sqrt{\|\delta_{\eta_x}(Z)\|_F^2+\|r\|_2^2}
 \ge\ell\min\{c_{\eta_x},1\}\,
 \operatorname{dist}\bigl((Z,r),\mathcal Z_\star^{\eta_x}\times\{0\}\bigr),
\]
and since $\Phi$ is affine with
$a_\Phi\operatorname{dist}(w,\mathcal W_\star)\le\operatorname{dist}(\Phi w,\Phi\mathcal W_\star)\le b_\Phi\operatorname{dist}(w,\mathcal W_\star)$
and transformed displacement $\mathsf M_\Phi\delta_{\mathrm P}(w)$, one may
take $c_{\mathrm P}=(a_\Phi/b_\Phi)\,\ell\min\{c_{\eta_x},1\}$ and
$t_{\mathrm P}=t_{\eta_x}/b_\Phi$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:pdhg-metric}
If $\theta:=\sqrt{\eta_x\eta_y}\,\lVert \mathcal A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}<1$, then $T_{\mathrm P}$ is
firmly nonexpansive in
$\mathsf G_{\mathrm P}:=\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}\eta_x^{-1}\mathrm{Id}&\mathcal A^*\\
\mathcal A&\eta_y^{-1}I_m\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]\succ0$, and one may take
$m_{\mathrm P}=(1-\theta)/\max\{\eta_x,\eta_y\}$ and
$M_{\mathrm P}=(1+\theta)/\min\{\eta_x,\eta_y\}$ in
\cref{lem:averaged-eb}.

name: PDHG parameter-dependent metric

title: Proof
body_md:
The cross term obeys
$2|\langle \mathcal A X,\lambda\rangle|\le\theta(\eta_x^{-1}\lVert X\rVert_F^2+\eta_y^{-1}
\lVert \lambda\rVert_2^2)$, which gives the metric bounds. Let
$\mathcal M(X,\lambda):=\bigl(C-\mathcal A^*\lambda+N_{\mathbb S_+^p}(X),\
\mathcal A X-b\bigr)$, a monotone operator: its off-diagonal linear part is
skew-adjoint and the normal cone is monotone. Direct substitution from the
PDHG update gives $0\in\mathcal M(w^+)+\mathsf G_{\mathrm P}(w^+-w)$, the
preconditioned proximal-point form of
PDHG~\cite{chambolle11jmiv-pdhg,oconnor20mp-pdhg-drs}; monotonicity applied
to two such inclusions gives
$\|w^+-\bar w^+\|_{\mathsf G_{\mathrm P}}^2\le
\langle w^+-\bar w^+,w-\bar w\rangle_{\mathsf G_{\mathrm P}}$, which is firm
nonexpansiveness.

title: Proof
body_md:
Define the point indicators
$\ell_a(x):=2^{-n}\prod_{i=1}^n(1+a_ix_i)
=2^{-n}\sum_{T\subseteq[n]}a^Tx^T$. Modulo $I_{\mathrm B}$,
$\ell_a^2\equiv\ell_a$ and $\sum_a\ell_a\equiv1$. At full order the moment
PSD condition tests the square of every Boolean function, so
$\pi_a:=L_y(\ell_a)=L_y(\ell_a^2)\ge0$ and $\sum_a\pi_a=1$; the
interpolation identity $h\equiv\sum_ah(a)\ell_a$ gives
$L_y(h)=\sum_a\pi_ah(a)$, i.e.\ the simplex representation. The vectors
$b_n(a)$ are mutually orthogonal because
$b_n(a)^\top b_n(b)=\prod_i(1+a_ib_i)=2^n\mathbf 1_{\{a=b\}}$, which proves
uniqueness of the coefficients and, for uniquely minimized $f$, uniqueness
of the optimal Dirac lift.

For upward persistence, an order-$d$ optimizer truncates to an order-$d_0$
feasible matrix with the same objective value ($\deg f\le2d_0$), and
hierarchy monotonicity with the feasible lift of $x_\star$ gives
$p_{d_0}(f)\le p_d(f)\le f(x_\star)=p_{d_0}(f)$; so the truncation is the
unique lower-order optimum, and in particular $y_{\{i\}}=x_{\star,i}$ for
all $i$. Choose Gram vectors $g_A$ of the higher-order optimizer with
$\langle g_A,g_B\rangle=y_{A\triangle B}$ and $\|g_A\|=1$. Whenever
$A,A\triangle\{i\}\in\mathcal I_d$,
$\langle g_A,g_{A\triangle\{i\}}\rangle=x_{\star,i}\in\{\pm1\}$, so equality in
Cauchy--Schwarz gives $g_{A\triangle\{i\}}=x_{\star,i}\,g_A$; adding the
elements of $A$ one at a time gives $g_A=x_\star^A\,g_\emptyset$, hence the
optimizer is $b_d(x_\star)b_d(x_\star)^\top$.

For the certificate: with $g:=f-f(x_\star)$ and $c_a:=2^{-n}b_n(a)$, set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:full-sc}
 S_{\mathrm{full}}:=\sum_{a\ne x_\star} g(a)\,c_ac_a^\top .
\end{equation}
One has $b_n(x)^\top c_ac_a^\top b_n(x)\equiv\ell_a(x)^2$, so
$S_{\mathrm{full}}$ represents
$\sum_{a\ne x_\star}g(a)\ell_a^2\equiv\sum_ag(a)\ell_a\equiv g$; all
displayed weights $g(a)$ are positive by unique minimality, and
orthogonality of the $b_n(a)$ gives
$\ker(S_{\mathrm{full}})=\operatorname{span}\{b_n(x_\star)\}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Openness.} Fix $g\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sc}}(a,d)$ with certificate $S$
positive definite on $u^\perp$, smallest restricted eigenvalue $\mu>0$. For
$h\in\mathcal Q(a,d)$, the matrix $S+\mathscr B_{a,d}(h)$ still annihilates $u$ and
represents $g+h$; by \eqref{eq:section-bound} it stays positive definite on
$u^\perp$ whenever $\lVert h\rVert_{\mathrm{coef}}<\mu/(2\sqrt{|\mathcal I_{2d}|-1})$, so
$g+h\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sc}}(a,d)$.

\emph{Density.} If $g\in\mathcal C(a,d)$, primal Slater gives an optimal Gram
matrix $S\succeq0$ representing $g$, and $u^\top Su=g(a)=0$ forces $Su=0$.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, $S+\varepsilon S_{\mathrm{int}}$ represents $g+\varepsilon r_{a,d}$
and is positive definite on $u^\perp$, so
$g+\varepsilon r_{a,d}\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sc}}(a,d)\to g$.

\emph{Semialgebraicity.} With $P_{u^\perp}=I_N-uu^\top/N$, membership in
$\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sc}}(a,d)$ is the existential first-order formula
$\exists S,t:\ \mathcal G_d(S)=g,\ Su=0,\ S-tP_{u^\perp}\succeq0,\ t>0$ (PSD-ness
being finitely many minor inequalities), and membership in $\mathcal C(a,d)$ is
$g\in\mathcal Q(a,d)$ and
$\nexists X\in\mathcal X_d:\ \lVert X-uu^\top\rVert_F^2>0,\ \langle C_g,X\rangle\le0$. The
Tarski--Seidenberg theorem and closure under complements make both cells
semialgebraic~\cite{bochnak98book-rag}.

\emph{Dimension.} Let $A=\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sc}}(a,d)$ and $B=\mathcal C(a,d)$; density
gives $A\subseteq B\subseteq\operatorname{cl} A$. The semialgebraic frontier theorem gives
$\dim(\operatorname{cl} A\setminus A)<\dim A$ and
$\dim\operatorname{cl} A=\dim A$~\cite[Propositions~2.8.2 and~2.8.13]{bochnak98book-rag},
so $\dim(B\setminus A)<\dim B$; and the open neighborhood of $r_{a,d}$
shows $\dim B=\dim\mathcal Q(a,d)=|\mathcal I_{2d}|-1$. The exceptional set therefore has
zero Lebesgue measure in $\mathcal Q(a,d)$.

There is an open dense full-measure semialgebraic set
$\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}\subseteq\mathcal P_n$ such that every $f\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}$ has a unique Boolean
minimizer and, at every order $d_\star(f)\le d\le n$, the relaxation admits

name: Simultaneous SC at every uniquely rank-one exact order

title: Proof
body_md:
First exclude the finite union of proper tie hyperplanes
$E_{\mathrm{tie}}:=\bigcup_{a\ne b}\{f:f(a)=f(b)\}$; each is proper because
some linear monomial distinguishes $a$ from $b$. For each pair $(a,d)$, let
$B_{a,d}:=\mathcal C(a,d)\setminus\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sc}}(a,d)$ and lift it to the full
coefficient space by the additive constant,
$\widetilde B_{a,d}:=\{g+c:g\in B_{a,d},\ c\in\mathbb R\}$. The map
$(g,c)\mapsto g+c$ is injective on this domain (because $g(a)=0$ recovers
$c=f(a)$), so for nonempty $B_{a,d}$,
\[
 \dim\widetilde B_{a,d}=\dim B_{a,d}+1<|\mathcal I_{2d}|\le2^n
\]
by \cref{thm:cell-generic}. Let $E$ be the union of $E_{\mathrm{tie}}$ with
the finitely many $\widetilde B_{a,d}$, and set
$\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}:=\mathcal P_n\setminus\operatorname{cl} E$. Finite unions and closures preserve
semialgebraicity and dimension, so $\dim\operatorname{cl} E<2^n$ and $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is open,
dense, and full measure. For $f\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{gen}}$ with minimizer $x_\star$,
\cref{prop:eventual} gives $d_\star(f)\le n$ and unique rank-one exactness
at every order $d\in[d_\star(f),n]$; at each such order,
$f-f(x_\star)\in\mathcal C(x_\star,d)$, and since $f$ avoids the corresponding
lifted bad set, this normalized objective lies in
$\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sc}}(x_\star,d)$.
